text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Planes collide near New Delhi. Over 300 feared dead.

- Finance Minister Lino Spiteri makes first visit to Malta Financial Services Centre, saying there is no atmosphere of uncertainty in business. It was business as usual under the new Labour government. He confirms John Bannister as chairman of the centre.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant meets Chamber of Commerce officials and tells them economy must be based on the private sector.
- General Workers Union presents memorandum on VAT. The new Labour government has promised to remove Value Added Tax within six months, a move the GWU supports.

- More searches planned for five-seat Piper Lance aircraft which crashed on way to Malta last December off Tunisia. Renewed search last month, after fishermen reported finding remains, was called off because of bad weather.
